저희.e: Humble version of 우리 — use with elders or customers: 저희 회사 'our company'.
저희.t: 저희 excludes the listener. For 'our country', always say 우리나라, never 저희 나라.

어느.forms: 어느 + noun: 어느 나라 · 어느 것 (어느 거) · 어느 쪽
어느.e: 어느 나라 사람이에요? 'Which country are you from?' — a classic first question.

아빠.x: Dad, are you coming home early today?
아빠.e: Casual word for 아버지 — many adults keep using it too.

저금하다.x: I save half of my salary every month.

가구.x: I bought new furniture for my new place.

장학금.x: My grades were good, so I got a scholarship.

남다.ex: 어제 먹고 남은 피자가 냉장고에 있어요.
남다.x: There's leftover pizza from yesterday in the fridge.
남다.e: Add -기- to get 남기다 'to leave something over'.

언어.ex: 저는 세 가지 언어를 할 수 있어요.

우표.ex: 편지 봉투에 우표를 붙이고 우체국에 갔어요.
우표.x: I put a stamp on the envelope and went to the post office.

몸살.m: body aches (with fatigue or chills), general achiness
몸살.ex: 어제 너무 무리해서 오늘 몸살이 났어요.
몸살.x: I overdid it yesterday, so today I'm achy all over.
몸살.e: Built on 몸 'body': aching all over, usually from exhaustion or a coming cold.
몸살.t: Say 몸살이 나다 or 몸살에 걸리다; English has no single word for it.

암기.x: I'm not good at memorizing vocabulary.
암기.e: Literally 'recording in the dark' — keeping it in your head without looking.
암기.t: In conversation, people usually say 외우다; 암기 sounds more like study talk.

삶.ex: 그는 아이들을 위해 바쁜 삶을 살았어요.
삶.x: He lived a busy life for his children.
삶.e: From 살다 'to live' + -ㅁ, a noun-making ending.
삶.t: Pronounced [삼]; the ㄹ in ㄻ is silent before a consonant or at the end.

시차.ex: 한국과 미국은 시차가 커서 전화하기 힘들어요.
시차.x: There's a big time difference between Korea and the US, so it's hard to call.
시차.t: For jet lag, say 시차 적응이 안 돼요, literally 'I can't adjust to the time difference.'

가리키다.m: to point at, to point to; to indicate, to refer to
가리키다.x: The child pointed at the sky with a tiny finger.
가리키다.t: Don't confuse 가리키다 'to point' with 가르치다 'to teach'; even natives mix them up.

전날.m: the day before, the previous day
전날.ex: 시험 전날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
전날.x: It's good to go to bed early the day before an exam.

이체하다.ex: 어제 먹은 밥값을 친구에게 이체해 줬어요.
이체하다.x: I transferred my share of yesterday's meal to my friend.

환기하다.x: After cooking, open the windows and air out the room.

스타.ex: 그 배우는 드라마 한 편으로 스타가 됐어요.
스타.x: That actor became a star from a single drama.

지사.x: That company has a branch office in the US too.
지사.e: Literally 'branch company' — a branch off the main trunk.
지사.t: 지사 is a company's regional office; 지점 is a local branch of a bank or store.

수요.x: In summer, demand for air conditioners rises sharply.
수요.t: Don't confuse with 수요일 (Wednesday) — 수 there means 'water'.

나눔.ex: 연말에는 이웃과 나눔을 실천하는 사람들이 많아요.
나눔.x: At the end of the year, many people practice sharing with their neighbors.
나눔.e: Noun made from 나누다 'to divide, to share' + -ㅁ.

절도.ex: 요즘 우리 동네에서 절도 사건이 자주 일어나요.
절도.x: Thefts have been happening often in our neighborhood lately.
절도.t: Formal or legal word, pronounced [절또]; in daily speech people say 도둑질 or 훔치다.

교과.ex: 이 내용은 고등학교 교과에 포함되어 있어요.
교과.x: This content is included in the high school curriculum.

뻔뻔하다.x: Even after lying, he smiled shamelessly.
뻔뻔하다.t: 뻔뻔스럽다 means the same thing and is equally common.

근사하다.x: We had dinner at a fancy restaurant on our anniversary.
근사하다.e: Literally 'close to resembling' — now mostly means 'impressively nice'.
근사하다.t: In everyday speech it means stylish or fancy; 'approximate' (근삿값) is a math term.

깔끔하다.ex: 방이 깔끔하게 정리되어 있어서 기분이 좋아요.
깔끔하다.x: It feels good because the room is neatly organized.
깔끔하다.t: Also praises food: 국물 맛이 깔끔해요 means the broth tastes clean, not greasy.

잔잔하다.x: There's no wind today, so the sea is calm.
잔잔하다.e: The doubled syllable paints a soft, steady stillness, like 촘촘하다 or 팽팽하다.

규율.x: In the military, you have to follow the rules strictly.
규율.e: Literally 'rule and law': the order a group must follow.
규율.t: This suffix is read 율 after a vowel or ㄴ, but 률 after other batchim, as in 법률.

첨부하다.x: I attached the report file to the email.
첨부하다.t: Common email line: 첨부 파일을 확인해 주세요 'Please see the attached file.'

고음.ex: 이 노래는 고음이 어려워서 노래방에서 못 불러요.
고음.x: The high notes in this song are hard, so I can't sing it at karaoke.
고음.e: Literally 'high sound'; the opposite is 저음 'low sound'.
고음.t: 'Hit a high note' is 고음을 내다; 고음이 안 올라가요 means 'I can't reach the high notes.'

쇄신.x: The party leadership promised a strong overhaul.

허위.ex: 그는 허위 사실을 퍼뜨린 혐의로 고소당했습니다.
허위.x: He was sued for spreading false information.

궤변.ex: 그런 궤변으로는 아무도 설득할 수 없어요.
궤변.x: You can't convince anyone with that kind of twisted logic.

불공정.ex: 불공정 거래를 막기 위해 법을 강화했습니다.
불공정.x: The law was strengthened to prevent unfair trade.
불공정.t: The prefix 불/부 'not' is read 부 before ㄷ or ㅈ (부족, 부정) and 불 elsewhere (불공정, 불편).

예후.ex: 의사는 수술 후 예후가 좋다고 말했어요.
예후.x: The doctor said the prognosis after surgery is good.
예후.t: Usually paired with 좋다 or 나쁘다: 예후가 좋다 (the outlook is good).

해체하다.m: to dismantle, to take apart; to disband
해체하다.ex: 회사는 낡은 건물을 해체하고 새로 지었습니다.
해체하다.x: The company tore down the old building and built a new one.
해체하다.e: Literally 'loosen the body' — taking something apart.
해체하다.t: Also used for K-pop groups breaking up: 그룹이 해체되다.

무해하다.x: They say this product is harmless to children.

덤덤하다.x: He stayed calm even after hearing the bad news.
덤덤하다.e: A doubled syllable word; the stronger form is 무덤덤하다 'totally unmoved'.
덤덤하다.t: Also used for food: 맛이 덤덤하다 'it tastes bland'.

명실상부하다.m: living up to its name; truly so, in name and in fact
명실상부하다.x: He is truly, in every sense, Korea's best actor.
명실상부하다.e: Literally 'name and reality match each other.'
명실상부하다.t: The opposite of 유명무실; usually 명실상부한 + noun or 명실상부하게.

빛 좋은 개살구.forms: 빛 좋은 개살구다 · 빛 좋은 개살구 같다
빛 좋은 개살구.m: all show and no substance; looks good but disappoints
빛 좋은 개살구.ex: 그 회사는 겉으로는 화려하지만 빛 좋은 개살구예요.
빛 좋은 개살구.x: That company looks glamorous on the outside, but it's all show and no substance.
빛 좋은 개살구.e: 개살구 is a wild apricot: bright-colored but sour. 개- often means 'wild, inferior.'

발단.m: the beginning, the origin, what started it (often of trouble)
발단.ex: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 발단이 되었어요.
발단.x: A small misunderstanding was what started a big fight.
발단.e: Literally 'start from the tip' — the first end of a thread.
발단.t: In literature class, 발단 is also 'exposition', the first stage of a plot: 발단–전개–위기–절정–결말.

멸종 위기종.x: The tiger is a typical endangered species.
멸종 위기종.t: 멸종 is pronounced [멸쫑] — tensification after ㄹ.

발뺌하다.m: to deny involvement, wriggle out of responsibility
발뺌하다.x: Even after the evidence came out, he kept denying it to the end.
발뺌하다.e: 발 'foot' + 빼다 'to pull out': pulling your foot out of a matter.

폭염 특보.ex: 폭염 특보가 내려져서 오늘 야외 행사가 취소됐어요.
폭염 특보.x: A heat wave alert was issued, so today's outdoor event was canceled.
폭염 특보.e: 폭염 'heat wave' (literally 'violent heat') + 특보 'special report, bulletin'.
폭염 특보.t: Pronounced [포겸 특뽀]. 폭염 특보 is the umbrella term for the milder 폭염 주의보 (advisory) and the more serious 폭염 경보 (warning). Alerts are 내려지다 'issued' and 해제되다 'lifted'.

변증법.ex: 헤겔의 변증법은 흔히 정, 반, 합의 단계로 설명됩니다.
변증법.x: Hegel's dialectic is often explained as the stages of thesis, antithesis and synthesis.

비애.ex: 그 소설은 이민자의 비애를 잘 그렸어요.
비애.x: That novel captures the sorrow of immigrants well.
비애.t: Often in 'X의 비애' for the sad lot of a group, e.g. 직장인의 비애.

진균.x: Athlete's foot is a skin disease caused by a fungus.
진균.t: 진균 is the clinical term; in daily life people just say 곰팡이 (mold, fungus).

랜섬웨어.ex: 랜섬웨어에 감염되면 컴퓨터 파일을 열 수 없게 돼요.
랜섬웨어.x: If you're infected with ransomware, you can't open your computer files.

버선.ex: 한복을 입을 때는 하얀 버선을 신어요.
버선.x: When you wear hanbok, you put on white beoseon socks.
버선.e: Its upturned toe, 버선코, is a classic image for the curved eaves of hanok roofs.
버선.t: Like 양말, it takes 신다: 버선을 신다.

천우신조.m: divine help, a stroke of providence
천우신조.ex: 천우신조로 큰 사고에서 가족 모두 무사했어요.
천우신조.x: By a miracle, the whole family came through the serious accident unharmed.
천우신조.t: Typically 천우신조로 'by the grace of heaven'.

견리사의.m: thinking of what is right when seeing profit
견리사의.x: Public officials must put what is right before profit.
견리사의.e: From Confucius: 'when you see gain, think of what is right'.
견리사의.t: Pronounced [결리사의]; famous as calligraphy by independence fighter Ahn Jung-geun.

흠모하다.m: to admire, to adore, to look up to
흠모하다.x: Many young people admired that independence activist.
흠모하다.e: Literally 'revere and long for' — deep, respectful admiration.

고장난명.m: it takes two; you can't do it alone
고장난명.ex: 고장난명이라고, 혼자서는 이 일을 해낼 수 없어요.
고장난명.x: As they say, one hand can't clap; I can't do this alone.
고장난명.e: Literally 'a single palm can hardly make a sound'.
고장난명.t: Pronounced [고장난명]; the native saying 손뼉도 마주쳐야 소리가 난다 means the same.

누란지세.m: a precarious situation, on the brink of collapse
누란지세.ex: 당시 나라는 누란지세의 위기에 처해 있었습니다.
누란지세.x: At the time, the country faced a crisis as precarious as stacked eggs.
누란지세.e: Literally 'the state of stacked eggs': ready to topple any moment.
누란지세.t: Often in 누란지세에 처하다 'to be in a precarious situation'.
